translationRepairs: He was soon promoted to attendant in the Office of the Censorate.
He was soon promoted to supervising secretary.
稍遷給事中 names the Menxia supervising secretary, not a Censorate office; the proposal is right but the English field must not embed 給事中.
He was gradually promoted to attendant in the Office of the Censorate.
He was gradually promoted to supervising secretary.
The same 給事中 is not a Censorate post; keep ‘supervising secretary’ without the Chinese gloss in the literal English.
He was promoted to Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace.
He was promoted to Vice Director of the Luan Terrace.
遷鸞臺侍郎 is the Wu-Zhou Menxia vice-directorship, distinct from 鳳閣/Phoenix; drop the parenthetical 鸞臺侍郎 from the English replacement.
He was transferred to Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace.
He was transferred to Vice Director of the Luan Terrace.
Literal likewise mislabels 鸞臺 as Phoenix Terrace; use Luan Terrace alone without Chinese characters in the English field.
When Zhang Xi joined the government, Qiao—being of his faction—was dismissed to the post of Rector of the Imperial University.
When Zhang Xi joined the government, Qiao—being his sister's son—was dismissed to the post of Rector of the Imperial University.
嶠，其出也 uses kinship 出 for sister’s son (maternal nephew of Zhang Xi), not factional membership.
When Zhang Xi entered the government, Qiao, being of the same faction, was removed and made Rector of the Imperial University.
When Zhang Xi entered the government, Qiao, being his sister's son, was removed and made Rector of the Imperial University.
The same 其出也 requires ‘sister’s son’ in the literal; ‘same faction’ invents a political bond the Chinese does not state.
Now the common people are destitute and poor, without secure dwellings—they cannot keep the throne.
Now the common people are destitute and poor, without secure dwellings—one cannot keep the throne.
Following 何以守位曰仁, 不可以守位 is impersonal: the throne cannot be kept amid 百姓乏窶, not that the people themselves cannot keep it.
Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Secretariat.
Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor.
同中書門下平章事 is associate grand councilor rank, not a second Secretariat directorship; the idiomatic already has the correct title.
His father Jing served as Long Secretary of Wei Prefecture and was known as a talented official.
His father Jing served as Chief Administrator of Wei Prefecture and was known as a talented official.
魏州長史 is prefectural chief administrator (changshi); ‘Long Secretary’ misreads 長 as a place-name element.
His father Jing was Long Secretary of Wei Prefecture and was called a talented official.
His father Jing was Chief Administrator of Wei Prefecture and was called a talented official.
The same 長史 error in the literal; Chief Administrator restores the office title.
I ask that from the chancellor and the sons of directors of all ministries onward, all be given outer offices, together bringing peace to the hundred surnames, inner and outer mutually coordinated.
I ask that the sons of the chancellor and of the directors of all ministries all be given outer offices, together bringing peace to the hundred surnames, inner and outer mutually coordinated.
宰相及諸司長官子弟 means the sons of the chancellor and of ministry directors; ‘from the chancellor and the sons… onward’ misparses the modifier 子弟.
He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State.
He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
尚書右丞 is Right Vice Director in the Shangshu sheng (Department of State Affairs), not a ‘Ministry of State’.
He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State.
He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
Literal repeats the same institutional mislabel for 尚書右丞; Department of State Affairs is correct.
When Jiaozhi rebelled, Zangyong earned merit in defense; he was made Registrar in Zha Prefecture, promoted to Long Secretary of Qian Prefecture acting as military commissioner, and died at Shixing.

When Jiaozhi rebelled, Zangyong earned merit in defense; he was made Registrar in Zha Prefecture, promoted to Chief Administrator of Qian Prefecture acting as military commissioner, and died at Shixing.
遷黔州長史 again uses changshi ‘chief administrator’; ‘Long Secretary’ is the same mistranslation as in s0153.

When Jiaozhi rebelled, Zangyong had merit in defense; he was changed to Registrar in Zha Prefecture, promoted to Long Secretary of Qian Prefecture and acting military commissioner, and died at Shixing.

When Jiaozhi rebelled, Zangyong had merit in defense; he was changed to Registrar in Zha Prefecture, promoted to Chief Administrator of Qian Prefecture and acting military commissioner, and died at Shixing.
Literal 黔州長史 requires Chief Administrator, not Long Secretary.
Sima Chengzhen once summoned him to court; as he was about to return to the mountains, Zangyong pointed to Zhongnan and said, "There are many fine places here".
Sima Chengzhen was once summoned to court; as he was about to return to the mountains, Zangyong pointed to Zhongnan and said, "There are many fine places here".
司馬承禎嘗召至闕下 makes Chengzhen the one summoned to court; the original reverses agent and patient.
Sima Chengzhen once summoned him to the palace; as he was about to return to the mountains, Zangyong pointed to Zhongnan and said: "Within this there are many fine places".
Sima Chengzhen was once summoned to the palace; as he was about to return to the mountains, Zangyong pointed to Zhongnan and said: "Within this there are many fine places".
The same 召至闕下 is passive of Chengzhen’s summons; ‘was once summoned’ corrects the reversed subject.
Wei Juyuan was of the same lineage as Wei Anshi and great-great-grandson of Zong, Metropolitan Governor under the Later Zhou.
Wei Juyuan was of the same lineage as Wei Anshi and great-grandson of Zong, Metropolitan Governor under the Later Zhou.
總曾孫 is great-grandson (generation distance 3); great-great-grandson would be 玄孫.
Wei Juyuan was of the same lineage as Anshi and great-great-grandson of Zong, Metropolitan Governor of the Later Zhou.
Wei Juyuan was of the same lineage as Anshi and great-grandson of Zong, Metropolitan Governor of the Later Zhou.
Literal likewise overstates 曾孫 as great-great-grandson; great-grandson matches the kinship term.
Yanzhao asked where the plan came from; Lüwen then asked Princess Anle to keep him, and General Yang Ju was substituted.
Yanzhao asked what plan to adopt; Lüwen then asked Princess Anle to keep him, and General Yang Ju was substituted.
問計安出 asks what stratagem to put forth, not whence a plan came; the proposal’s sense is right, but ‘what plan there was’ is awkward—‘what plan to adopt’ is clearer.
He once wore women's dress and rode in a carriage with his wife to call together—the shaman's power gained him the chancellorship.
He once wore women's dress and rode in a carriage with his wife to pay a visit together—the shaman's power gained him the chancellorship.
與妻偕謁 means he and his wife paid a visit together (to the shaman of s0242); ‘call together’ loses the sense of 謁.
He Fengyao was a native of Qi in Qi Prefecture.
He Fengyao was a native of Qishan in Qi Prefecture.
岐州岐山人 names Qishan county within Qi Prefecture; bare ‘Qi’ drops 岐山 and duplicates the prefecture.
He Fengyao was a man of Qi in Qi Prefecture.
He Fengyao was a man of Qishan in Qi Prefecture.
The same 岐山 requires Qishan in the literal native-place formula.
Fengyao, because the mission had purpose, was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
Fengyao, because the mission achieved its aim, was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
以使有指 means the embassy achieved its intended aim (指), after Mochuo’s submission in s0261; ‘had purpose’ understates the success.
